operator_io_quirks: Mixed DDL style: customer uses backtick-quoted identifiers and inline `PRIMARY KEY (...)`/`FOREIGN KEY ... ON DELETE CASCADE`; other tables use bare identifiers and lowercase `primary key`/`foreign key` — line-based unique/check scan must tolerate both.

Huge tables: lineitem 4.42M rows, orders 1.5M, partsupp 800k, part 200k, customer 150k — rowid%k sampling mandatory; original_values for these columns will be sampled, original_sizes must still be full count(*).

lineitem has a COMPOSITE FK (l_partkey,l_suppkey)->partsupp(ps_partkey,ps_suppkey); pragma foreign_key_list reports it as two separate rows (id shared) — the fks dict keyed by single (child_t,child_c) will hold two independent edges, losing the pairing.
lineitem PK is composite (l_orderkey,l_linenumber); partsupp PK composite (ps_partkey,ps_suppkey) — composite-PK members get max_l0=30, not inf.

DATE columns (l_shipdate, l_commitdate, l_receiptdate, o_orderdate) are declared DATE but stored as TEXT 'YYYY-MM-DD' — Date fuzzer with template %Y-%m-%d; first element does not parse as int so Date branch, not Number.
All null_rate = 0.0 across every column despite many `DEFAULT NULL` / nullable declarations — original_values contain no NULLs; TS base drops None anyway.
o_shippriority has distinct=1 (all '0') — String/Number sampler with a single element; Number list range collapses.
c_phone/s_phone are TEXT with format 'NNN-NNN-NNNN' (distinct ~= row count) — String fuzzer will not reproduce the dash pattern; only literal-pool values from train SQL carry it.

c_name/s_name/o_clerk/p_brand/p_mfgr are TEXT with '#'-embedded patterns ('Customer#000000001', 'Brand#43', 'Clerk#000000916') — String fuzzer's int-like +1/-1 rule may fire on the numeric tail only if the whole string parses as int (it does not), so these stay opaque strings.
FKs all resolve to existing parents (no dangling); nation/region are tiny (25/5 rows) so FK child draws from parent final values will heavily repeat — ties/duplicates expected.

No self-references, no non-unique FK parents (all FK targets are PKs), no missing parents — clean FK graph; topological order is a simple DAG region->nation->{customer,supplier}->orders->lineitem, part->partsupp->lineitem.

REAL columns (c_acctbal, l_extendedprice, o_totalprice, p_retailprice, ps_supplycost, s_acctbal) have negative values (c_acctbal -926.96) — Number full range [-10^scale,10^scale] with scale from `REAL` (no args -> scale default) will produce plausible magnitudes.
operator_ts_expectations: Date fuzzer on l_shipdate/l_commitdate/l_receiptdate/o_orderdate: template %Y-%m-%d, range from min/max parsed originals (~1992-1998), so fresh dates stay in that window — good for range predicates, but no dates outside 1992-1998 (misses on 'before 1992' style queries).

String fuzzer on c_mktsegment/l_returnflag/l_linestatus/l_shipmode/l_shipinstruct/o_orderpriority/o_orderstatus/p_container/p_type: 5 original samples + distinct literal-pool values, p=0.2 fresh random CHARSET strings — fresh values are implausible ('aB3 ()'), driving FN on equality/IN predicates over these enums.

Number fuzzer on l_discount/l_tax (REAL, distinct 11/9): list range [min(el), 10^scale] with the upstream overwrite quirk — fresh draws can exceed 1.0, so 'discount between 0.05 and 0.07' may see out-of-range values (FP risk on range predicates).
Number fuzzer on l_quantity (INTEGER, distinct 50, values 1-50): full range [-10^scale,10^scale] with scale from INTEGER (no args) — fresh ints far outside 1-50, FN on 'quantity < 10' style.

Number fuzzer on PKs (c_custkey, o_orderkey, p_partkey, s_suppkey, ps_partkey, ps_suppkey, l_orderkey, l_linenumber, n_nationkey, r_regionkey): single-col PK -> max_l0=inf, so fresh draws never reused; composite members capped at 30 — PKs stay unique-ish but values unrelated to original ranges.

FK consistency: o_custkey drawn from customer final c_custkey; l_orderkey from orders final o_orderkey; l_partkey/l_suppkey drawn INDEPENDENTLY from partsupp.ps_partkey/ps_suppkey (composite FK pairing lost) — join predicates on (l_partkey,l_suppkey)=(ps_partkey,ps_suppkey) will mostly fail (FN).
Tiny parents (region 5, nation 25): FK child columns n_regionkey, c_nationkey, s_nationkey get heavy duplicate draws — ties present, good for GROUP BY/COUNT DISTINCT, but distinct counts collapse.
o_shippriority single value '0': Number sampler with 1 element -> list range degenerate, fresh draws from full range — 'shippriority = 0' predicates may see nonzero (FP).

String fuzzer on c_comment/l_comment/o_comment/ps_comment/s_comment/n_comment/r_comment/p_comment (long text, distinct ~= rows): fresh random strings of length 0-20 + contaminate — LIKE '%express%' predicates will mostly miss (FN), but substring spans from neighbor_queries may hit.
p_retailprice REAL distinct 20899 with values 901.0,902.0,... (near-integer): Number float perturb +-0.01/+-0.02 — 'retailprice = 901' equality may see 900.99/901.01 (FP).
c_phone/s_phone TEXT 'NNN-NNN-NNNN': String fuzzer fresh strings lack dashes; literal pool from train SQL may carry a few phone literals — LIKE '%-%' predicates fragile.

No CHECK constraints, no UNIQUE columns beyond PKs — drop_unique_duplicates is a no-op here; NOT NULL on many columns (l_discount, l_extendedprice, l_quantity, l_tax, l_orderkey, l_linenumber, l_partkey, l_suppkey, o_custkey, c_custkey, ps_* keys) — TS does not enforce NOT NULL in Python, so NULLs from empty-parent FK draws or String allow_none would fail at insert and be skipped (row loss).
